title: Stride Bank, N.A. Privacy Policy
text: Last updated: January 2025 This notice describes how we collect, use and share information. Other privacy policies may apply in addition to the terms of this notice. If you inquire about, apply for, or have a financial product or service with us, please review our Privacy Notice , which applies to U.S. customers and consumers as described in that notice. Collecting and Using Information This section generally describes how Stride Bank collects and uses your personal information, and how Stride Bank may use your personal information. Personal information generally means information that identifies you or your device, and other information we associate with it. Why? Financial companies choose how they share your personal information.Federal law gives consumers the right to limit some but not all sharing. Federal law also requires us to tell you how we collect, share, and protect your personal information. Please read this notice carefully to understand what we do. What? The types of personal information we collect and share depend on the product or service you have with us. This information can include: Social Security number Account balances and transaction history Account transactions and risk tolerance When you are no longer our customer, we continue to share your information as described in this notice. How? All financial companies need to share customers’ personal information to run their everyday business. In the section below, we list the reasons financial companies can share their customers’ personal information; the reasons Stride Bank, N.A. chooses to share; and whether you can limit this sharing. Reasons we can share your personal information Does Stride Bank, N.A. Share? Can you limit this sharing? For our everyday business purposes— such as to process your transactions, maintain your account(s), respond to court orders and legal investigations, or report to credit bureaus Yes No For our marketing purposes— to offer our products and services to you Yes No For joint marketing with other financial companies No For our affiliates’ everyday business purposes— information about your transactions and experiences No We don't share For our affiliates’ everyday business purposes— information about your creditworthiness No We don't share For our affiliates to market to you No We don't share For non-affiliates to market to you No We don't share Questions If you have any questions, please contact us by completing the Albert Privacy Rights Request form at https://albertapp.typeform.com/to/soPYKo. You may also contact us at the “Contact Support” link in the help center section of the App, or by email at privacy@albert.com. Who we are Who is providing this notice? Stride Bank, N.A. What we do How does Stride Bank, N.A. protect my personal information? To protect your personal information from unauthorized access and use, we use security measures that comply with federal law. These measures include computer safeguards and secured files and buildings. How does Stride Bank, N.A. collect my personal information? We collect your personal information, for example, when you open an account or deposit money pay your bills or give us your contact information use your credit or debit card We also collect your personal information from other companies. Why can’t I limit all sharing? Federal law gives you the right to limit only sharing for affiliates’ everyday business purposes—information about your creditworthiness affiliates from using your information to market to you sharing for non-affiliates to market to you State laws and individual companies may give you additional rights to limit sharing. See below for more on your rights under state law. Definitions Affiliates Companies related by common ownership or control. They can be financial and nonfinancial companies. Stride Bank, N.A. has no affiliates with which it shares your personal information. Nonaffiliates Companies not related by common ownership or control. They can be financial and nonfinancial companies. Stride Bank, N.A. does not share with non-affiliates so they can market to you. Joint marketing A formal agreement between nonaffiliated financial companies that together market financial products or services to you. We do not jointly market bank products with other financial companies. Other important information Vermont Residents: In accordance with Vermont law, we will not share with non-affiliates except for our own marketing purposes, our everyday business purposes, or with your consent. Nevada Residents: Nevada law requires that we provide you with the following contact information: Bureau of Consumer Protection, Office of the Nevada Attorney General, 555 E. Washington Ave., Suite 3900, Las Vegas, NV 89101; Phone number: 702-486-3132; email: agInfo@ag.nv.gov California Residents: Effective January 1, 2020, the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) permits consumers who are California residents to (a) ask a covered business which categories and pieces of personal information it collects and how the information is used; (b) request deletion of the information; and (c) opt out of the sale of such information, if applicable. These provisions of the CCPA do not apply to personal information collected, processed, shared, or disclosed by financial institutions pursuant to federal law. To contact us with questions about our compliance with the CCPA, please contact us by completing the Albert Privacy Rights Request form at https://albertapp.typeform.com/to/soPYKo. You may also contact us at the “Contact Support” link in the help center section of the App, or by email at privacy@albert.com. Only you or a person registered with the California Secretary of State that you authorize to act on your behalf, may make a verifiable consumer request related to your personal information. You may also make a verifiable consumer request on behalf of your minor child. You may make a verifiable consumer request to know or delete personal information twice within a 12-month period. We endeavor to respond to a verifiable consumer request within 45 days of its receipt. If we require more time (up to 90 days), we will inform you of the reason and extension period in writing. Any disclosures we provide will only cover the preceding 12-month period. The response we provide will also explain the reasons we cannot comply with a request, if applicable. For right to know requests, we will select a format to provide your personal information that is readily useable and should allow you to transmit the information from one entity to another entity without hindrance. We do not charge a fee to process or respond to your verifiable consumer request unless it is excessive, repetitive, or manifestly unfounded. If we determine that the request warrants a fee, we will tell you why we made that decision and provide you with a cost estimate before completing your request. Please note, consumers will not receive discriminatory treatment for the exercise of the privacy rights conferred by the CCPA. Member FDIC

title: Albert Genius User Guidelines
text: Last updated: July 30, 2025 Albert Genius is a new type of financial assistant that uses generative AI to help you navigate your finances, set up a budget and financial plan, and answer general financial and other questions. You are expected to engage with Albert Genius in a responsible, legal, and safe manner. The following restrictions apply to your interactions with Albert Genius services and products. By accessing and using Albert Genius, you agree to abide by these User Guidelines. Do not engage in conduct that is unlawful, dangerous, or that could harm yourself or others. For example, do not use Albert Genius to: Promote or engage in any criminal activities, including the exploitation or harm of children; Promote or incite violence; Facilitate the production or distribution of sexually explicit content; Promote or facilitate self-harm; Violate the rights of others, including by using personal data or biometrics without legally-required consent; Engage in hate speech, harassment, bullying, intimidation, or abuse of others. Do not compromise the security of others’ or Albert’s services. Do not engage in or facilitate: Spam, phishing, or malware. Abuse of, harm to, interference with, or disruption to Albert’s or others’ infrastructure or services. Circumvention of abuse protections or safety filters, such as by manipulating the model to contravene our policies. Introduction of viruses, malware, ransomware and other destructive computer programs. Do not engage in conduct that could significantly impair the safety, wellbeing, or rights of others. For example, do not use Albert Genius to: Facilitate or engage in gambling, political campaigning, or lobbying; Provide medical, financial, tax, legal or other services that would typically require specialized credentials or licensing; Make automated decisions about individuals that could have a material detrimental impact on them; Track or monitor people without their consent; Provide services targeted to minors; Exploit vulnerabilities related to age, disability, or socioeconomic circumstances. Do not use Albert Genuis to intentionally deceive or mislead others. For example, do not: Engage in frauds, scams, or other deceptive actions. Impersonate an individual (living or dead) without consent or legal right. Generate or promote false or misleading information. Engage in academic dishonesty. Misrepresent the provenance of AI-generated content by claiming it was created by a human. There are many ways that you can engage with Albert Genius, and many ways Albert Genius can respond. This is because large language models, like the models used by Albert Genius, are probabilistic, which means they are always producing new and different responses to user inputs. Albert Genius’ outputs are informed by the large language models that it uses, which means that Albert Genius will sometimes reflect the limits of those models and may not always provide complete or accurate responses. Responses from Albert Genius may contain errors or omissions, and offer recommendations that could result in financial losses. You should always exercise your own judgment and confirm the output of Albert Genius before making any decisions and consult with your financial advisor or other professionals as appropriate. The responses generated by Albert Genius should not be construed as financial, legal or tax advice. We may modify these User Guidelines at any time to reflect changes in our practices, technology, legal requirements, or other factors. Your continued use of Albert Genius following the posting or notice of any changes will mean you accept those changes. If you have feedback or comments about using Albert Genius or the outputs that you receive from using it, we encourage you to let us know by emailing genius-feedback@albert.com . As we learn more about how our users use Albert Genius and find it most helpful, we may update these guidelines and reserve the right to do so, in whole or in part, at any time and from time to time.

title: How do loans with Albert work?
text: Personal loans are offered on Albert to customers who qualify to apply for a loan. Apply to see your loan amount, term, and repayment options in the app. What is a personal loan? A personal loan is a sum of money borrowed to pay for a variety of expenses, such as debt consolidation, home improvement projects, or other personal reasons. Many banks, credit unions, and lenders offer personal loans. The borrowed money must be repaid over time, typically with interest. Lenders may also charge additional fees. Are the loans fixed interest rate or variable interest rate loans? The loans are fixed interest rate loans. Your interest rate and monthly repayment amount is agreed to when you accept the loan and does not change for the full term of the loan. Are the loans secured or unsecured? The loans are unsecured, which means you are not required to provide collateral to get a loan. Common examples of collateral required with a secured loan include cash up front or secured with property such as a car. Why was I denied? If you're denied, we'll tell you why with a decline notice known as an "adverse action." This notice will include an overview of the reasons why you were declined. Additional information Albert Loans may be issued by FinWise Bank, a Utah chartered commercial bank, Member FDIC, or Albert, pursuant to licenses in Utah and Florida. For more information about the licenses Albert holds, see here . Albert does not discriminate against any credit applicant on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, marital status, age (providing the applicant is of legal age and has the capacity to enter into a binding legal contract), sex, disability, familial status, receipt of public assistance, or if the individual has exercised in good faith any right under the Consumer Credit Protection Act, or on any other prohibited basis.

title: How do I make payments on my loan?
text: You can make manual payments or turn on auto pay to repay your loan. How do I manage my payment details? To view or manage your loan payment details in the app: On the home screen, select profile (👤). Tap the menu icon in the top left (☰). Select "Payments." Under the "Loan payment details" section, select "Payment details." You can also contact support to temporarily pause or turn off auto pay at any time. How do I make a manual payment? You can make one-time payments manually in the app. Here's how: From the home screen, tap "Instant." Go to settings (⚙️). Under the loan section select "Make manual payment" Add the payment details. Tap "Make payment" and then "Confirm payment." We'll send you an email if your manual payment fails. You can only make payments equal to the exact amount due or the entire balance remaining on your loan. If you are behind on payments, you can make multiple payments at once (e.g. 3 months worth of payments). What happens if I miss a payment? If we don't receive a payment within 10 days after your due date, you may be charged a late fee. Late payments that are overdue by 30 days or more may be reported to the credit bureaus, which might negatively impact your credit score. If you have auto pay on but insufficient funds in your linked funding source, your automatic payment may not complete and your payment may become late. We'll send you an email if your payment is late.

title: How do loans impact my credit score?
text: Will applying for an Albert Loan impact my credit score? To check your rates, a soft credit pull is required. A soft pull may show up on your credit report, but it will not impact your credit score. If you choose to submit your application for a loan, we will request a hard credit pull from one or more consumer reporting agencies. A hard credit pull will show up on your credit report, and may impact your credit score. Will my loan payments be reported to the credit agencies? We report loan payments to at least one of the major credit bureaus as you repay your loan. Complete, on-time payments might help improve your credit score, but late or missed payments might negatively affect your score. Why do I see FinWise Bank or Albert on my Consumer Report? You may see FinWise Bank referenced on your consumer report if you applied for a loan through Albert that was originated by FinWise Bank. In some instances, loans may have been originated by Albert directly in which case you may see Albert referenced on your consumer report. Albert reports information about your loan (such as on-time, late, and missed payments; any defaults; and the fact you paid off your loan) to consumer reporting agencies (e.g. Experian, Transunion, and/or Equifax). Albert loans are issued by FinWise Bank, a Utah chartered commercial bank, Member FDIC.

title: Your privacy choices
text: When you use the Albert app or visit the Albert website, we may track information related to you or your device. This information may be shared with third parties to optimize your experience with Albert and to market our services. To change your sharing preferences Go to your Profile (👤). Tap the menu in the top corner (☰). Tap Security . Tap on Information sharing . Toggle Allow sharing on or off. You can also change these settings from a browser by visiting here and clicking on Data sharing permissions. To learn more about your privacy choices, visit our Privacy Policy .

title: Deactivating or closing your Albert account
text: You can deactivate your account to cancel your subscription, or close your account permanently. You do either from a web browser at albert.com/deactivate , or in the app. Deactivate account Deactivating your account will cancel your Albert subscription. Your login details will remain active and you can reactivate your subscription again at any time. You will continue to have access to any Albert features that aren't part of Albert's subscription. Requirements Any accounts included with your subscription must be zeroed out. Bring your Albert Savings and Investing balances to $0. This includes withdrawing all funds and selling any investments. Deactivating your account does not remove any advance or loan balances owed. If you have an outstanding advance or loan, you will need to continue to make payments to avoid additional fees. If you have auto pay on, we'll continue to make automatic payments on your balances owed. Permanent account closure Permanent account closure will close all of your Albert accounts. You won't be able to send or receive funds with your Albert account. Pending and future deposits, including direct deposits, that continue to get sent to your account will get returned, which may take a few days to process and complete. Requirements Any accounts included with your subscription must be zeroed out. Bring your Albert Savings and Investing balances to $0. This includes withdrawing all funds and selling any investments. Any additional accounts included with your Albert account must be zeroed out. Bring your Albert Cash balance to $0, and repay any outstanding advance or loan balances. To deactivate or close your account in the app: On the home screen, select profile (👤). Tap the menu icon in the top left (☰). Tap "Payments" Tap "Help center." Choose "Deactivate or close my accounts." You can also chat with our virtual support agent here for guided support deactivating or closing your account. For help bringing your balances to $0 Withdraw from Cash Withdraw from Savings Sell Investments Withdraw from Investing Repay Instant balance Repay Loan balance Pause Smart money deposits View the requirements above to see more on which balances must be $0 to deactivate or close your account.

title: Relinking account
text: For security purposes, If you’ve updated your username for your financial institution’s login recently, You will need to re-link this account as though it’s a new account. Please contact our support staff if you’re seeing an error related to an updated username on your account. They will be able to assist you in re-linking this account.

title: Can I get a refund for Albert Genius?
text: We do not offer refunds for monthly Albert subscriptions. Please note that pausing Smart money does not pause your Albert subscription payments. For help with deactivating or closing your account see here .

title: Albert account requirements
text: You must meet the following requirements in order to set an Albert account: Individual requirements Be a U.S. resident or citizen Be 18 years old or older Hold a bank account with a U.S. financial institution Technical requirements A mobile phone number and plan provided by a mobile carrier operating in the U.S. A mobile phone that supports the Albert mobile app (refer to our App Store and Google Play store descriptions for current specifications). Please note: While our aim is to help everyone make better financial decisions, we cannot support internet-based phone services (i.e., Google Voice) at this time.

title: Install the app and register
text: To create your Albert account, download the Albert app onto your mobile phone from the App Store. To register, open the app, enter your name, email address, and select a secure password. Passwords must be at least 8 characters long. Next, you must set a secure 4-digit PIN. This PIN serves as a layer of security and allows you to unlock your Albert account in case there are unauthorized attempts to access it. To complete account registration, you must confirm your identity by entering your mobile phone number. You’ll receive a 4-digit confirmation code via SMS. Enter this code into the app in order to authenticate your account. Albert does not support VoIP (voice over IP) phone numbers, such as Google Voice, in an effort to combat fraud.

title: I'm unable to connect to my financial institution
text: There are thousands of financial institutions in the U.S. Establishing connections with the computer systems across many institutions can be challenging. The reliability of these systems vary by institution, and each bank has its own rules and practices when it comes to security protocols, account authentication, and so on. In order to ensure that we’re able to access as many of these systems as possible, Albert (and most other financial services companies) partners with an account aggregator— Plaid —who has established direct connections with the computer systems at many financial institutions. However, not every financial institution supports online connections from third parties. Also, banks experience systems crashes, security protocols change, and other unforeseen circumstances arise. As a result, you may periodically be unable to connect to your financial institution account when accessing it from Albert. If this happens, see our troubleshooting article on common account linking errors . If you’re still having trouble connecting to your account, you may need to attempt connecting again later—many account connection issues tend to get resolved by the account aggregators and the banks within several hours to a day.

title: Tell us about you
text: We ask you a series of questions about yourself as part of the account registration process in order to understand more about you and your priorities. We do this in order to best serve your needs: a 19-year-old single student has different financial objectives and priorities than a 37-year-old professional with two kids who will be starting college soon.

title: Connect your financial accounts
text: To make the most of Albert's budgeting features, link your accounts so our algorithm gets a full picture of your financial life. Start with your primary checking account — the account where your paychecks and other income is deposited and from which you pay the bulk of your bills. Once you've connected your bank account, you can add others, including credit cards, loans (e.g., student loans, car loans, personal loans, or mortgages), and investments (e.g., brokerage, retirement, or 529 plans). The more accounts you add, the more helpful Albert can be! If your account is with a major bank, such as Chase or Bank of America, follow the below steps. To add a new financial account to Albert Go to the "Profile" tab (👤). Tap "Linked accounts." Tap "Add account." Select your financial institution or search for it by name if it’s not listed. Enter your financial institution account credentials. If you encounter an error when linking an account, please review the list of common account linking errors to find a solution. If your account is with a smaller institution, such as a regional bank or credit union that we don't currently support, add your account manually. Instructions for adding accounts manually are found here .

title: How does bill lowering work?
text: Bill lowering negotiation We can negotiate your bills for you. We cover a selection of cable, satellite TV, internet, and phone companies as well as and other service providers. Upload a photo of a bill in the app, and our team of negotiators will call your service provider to negotiate your bill down on your behalf. An Albert Cash account and Genius account fee are required to access bill lowering. To see if any bills are eligible to lower: Go to the "Overview" tab (📊). Scroll down to "Bills to lower." You'll see a list of bills we can help negotiate. Once you submit a bill, we’ll keep you updated on it’s progress. Check your email, or view the progress of your bill from the Overview tab. Each bill is different, so the likelihood of success and how much you could save is based on past outcomes from similar bills. In some cases our negotiators may not be able to lower your bill if you’re already paying the best rate.

title: Spending plan
text: Income Bills, debt repayment, and savings Spending money Building a budget Albert uses what we call a "spending plan," which takes the stress out of budgeting. No more wondering if you have enough for bills or savings throughout the month — with a spending plan, you take those into account first. Here’s how it works: Income : Your income is the total amount of funds you bring in each month. Bills, debt repayment, and savings : Add up everything you have to pay each month, like rent, credit card balances, and loans. Then, calculate your savings. Ideally, you should be saving no less than 10% of your monthly income — think of it as a bill you owe your future self! The best way to grow your savings is to set aside money immediately after receiving income. Spending money : That’s whatever income you have left after Step 2. Your spending money is yours to save, invest and spend on essentials (gas, groceries, etc) and non-essentials (shopping, dining out, entertainment, etc). If you have debt, put funds toward the debt. If you have an Albert Savings Goal, move funds there. Or use it for something else that brings you joy! The key here is not to go over the allocated amount in step 3. In the app, this labeled as "left to spend" in your budget. Often, it's only after we overspend on non-essentials that we realize we don’t have enough to save and then it goes to the next month. With a spending plan, you will need to accept this free spending money amount and stick to it. If you can do that, then you don't have to worry about if you're saving enough for your bills and goals any more or have guilt about spending your money how you please.

title: What are available funds?
text: To invest with Albert, you must first fund your account by depositing cash. Money held in your account for the purpose of investing is called available funds. These funds include any money you deposit, or any money you withdraw from an investment. Learn how to make a manual deposit here . Any cash you manually deposit will need to be allocated into your investments manually. When auto-investing is on, Albert automatically withdraws your preferred deposit amount and allocates it into your investments based on your preferences. To learn about setting up automated cash deposits, visit our article on auto-investing here . Your cash deposits must remain in your account for a minimum of 5 trading days before being available for withdrawal. This holding period is for anti-money laundering and risk management purposes. Albert will not initiate an automatic deposit if your funding bank account's balance is less than $200.

title: How do I sell an investment?
text: After your investment settles, you may sell it the following day. To sell an investment: On the home screen, tap "Investing." Tap the investment you want to sell. Tap settings ( ⚙️ ). Under "Investing," tap "Sell." Enter the dollar amount you want to sell in the "Amount to sell" field. Tap "Sell." Your investment will be sold within the next trading day. After Albert sells your investment, your proceeds from the sale will be deposited into your available cash in 2 days (Mon–Fri). You may withdraw it or reinvest it into another holding.

title: How do I withdraw available funds?
text: To withdraw available funds from Albert Investing: Go to the "Profile" tab. Tap "Transfer money." Choose "Investing" as the account you're sending money from. Choose the account you want to transfer money to. Type your transfer amount and hit "Transfer." Your Investing available balance only includes completed cash deposits. Pending deposits take up to 2 business days to settle before they can be withdrawn. You must wait 5 business days to withdraw any cash recently deposited into your Investing account. This holding period is for anti-money laundering and risk management purposes.

title: How do I set my investing allocation?
text: When you have Smart money turned on, Albert can automatically save and invest for you. Auto-deposits to your Investing account will be invested based on your allocation selection. This lets you choose what percentage of each deposit to invest in any individual stock, ETF, or strategies managed by Albert. Any unallocated cash will be deposited to your settlement fund. To adjust your Investing allocations: On the home screen, tap ”Investing.” Go to settings (⚙️). Scroll down to "Investment allocations." Tap ”Edit allocation.” Adjust the sliders to your desired allocation.

title: What are my documents?
text: Your documents are formal records of your investments with Albert. When you select holdings and make investments, you'll receive several documents related to your investments. Albert will notify you via email when your documents become available. To view your documents in the app: Tap Investing on the home screen. Tap the cog (⚙️) in the top right corner. Select Documents. Trade confirmations These documents confirm the trades you made in the past month. Trades refer to investments bought, as well as investments sold. Tax documents As an SEC-registered investment advisor, Albert Investments, LLC is mandated to send relevant tax documents to every investor. Keep these documents in a safe place, as you may need to disclose your investments on your taxes. As Albert does not provide tax advice or guidance, it's a good idea to consult your accountant (or whoever prepares your tax return) if you have any questions about reporting investments on your taxes. Monthly statements These are documents sent at month's end. They provide an overview of your trades and withdrawals, as well as your most recent account balance. Proxy documents When you make an investment in a company or fund through the purchase of stocks, bonds or other securities, you become an official shareholder in that company or fund. As a shareholder, you have the right to participate in votes on matters that may include: Elections, such as to the board of directors Corporate structural changes Mergers and acquisitions Executive compensation packages And more You will be notified of any upcoming shareholder votes as they occur. When Albert sends you information related to your proxy vote, we'll include a link to your proxy statement and the company's (or fund's) annual report. Such information is provided to help you make an informed decision when the date of the shareholder vote occurs. Your proxy vote is not mandatory. Prospectus documents are provided when you make an initial investment in stocks, bonds and other securities. These documents help you explore the companies or funds in which you've invested. A company's prospectus documents may include: A description of the type of investment made The company's or fund's history and financial information, along with information about its management The price and date of the investment Any selling discounts How the company will use your invested money Any risks involved A fund's prospectus will typically contain information about the fund's objectives, investment strategies, risks, performance, distribution policy, management and expenses. If you have any other questions about investment documents, or your rights as an investor, text Genius.

title: What are strategies managed by Albert?
text: When you sign up for Albert Investing, you can create a strategy managed by Albert that you can use to invest in the stock market. How it works: Tap ”Investing” on the home screen. Under Managed by Albert, tap “Add strategy.” Select your strategy. What's the difference between conservative, balanced, or growth strategies? Conservative Contains "lower-risk" investments; i.e., holdings that are less inclined to volatile performance, with the opportunity for smaller, steady gains. Balanced Contains "medium-risk" investments; i.e., holdings that have a chance of volatile performance, with the opportunity for moderate gains. Growth Contains "high-risk" investments; i.e., holdings that are more inclined to volatile performance, with the opportunity for significant gains. You can change your preferences at any time. You can also set different risk levels for different investments. Please keep in mind that all investments in securities involve a risk of loss. No method of investing, nor any type of investment, guarantees success.

title: The Albert referral program
text: We want to spread the word about Albert — so tell your friends! For every friend you invite to Albert, they’ll get access to advance $50 with Instant when they join Albert and set up Albert Instant Advances. See more below. How can I invite friends? Open the Albert app Go to the profile tab (👤) Tap “Invite friends” You’ll be prompted to sync your contacts Refer as many friends as you’d like! Heads up: we’ll never message your contacts without your permission. Requirements Your referral is not already an Albert member, Your referral signs up with your unique referral link within 10 days of sending the invite Your referral creates an Albert Cash account Your referral sets up Albert Instant Advances Your referral meets all of the above requirements within 45 days of joining Albert. Albert may edit the requirements for the Albert referral program at any time at its discretion including the Instant eligibility criteria. Still have questions? Contact support for help. Terms and Conditions The Referral Program described above is subject to these Terms and Conditions. Eligibility 1. Eligibility requirements are outlined in the “Requirements” section above. For additional clarity, your friend must also meet the criteria outlined in the “Requirements” section above in order to receive the promotional offer. 2. You can invite as many friends as you want; however, we reserve the right to limit the number of promotional offers you are eligible to send at our discretion. Limitations 1. The Instant offer for Albert members who join with a friend’s invite only applies to members who are exposed to the Referral Program in the App. The only offers owed to you for each referral and applicable qualification details are as described above or in the Referral Program section of the App. In the event you send your friend more than one referral link for different referral programs, your friend who meets the applicable eligibility criteria will only be entitled to the offer associated with the original referral link they used to download the App. 2. If you violate these Terms and Conditions or the terms of the Referral Program, you are automatically ineligible to receive any compensation under the Referral Program. 3. You agree and represent that you will not engage in any solicitation activities under the Referral Program that violate federal or state law, and that you are not subject to an SEC order issued under section 203(f) of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (“Advisers Act”), you have not been convicted within the past ten years of any felony or misdemeanor involving conduct described in section 203(e) of the Advisers Act, you have not been found by the SEC to have engaged, or have been convicted of engaging, in any of the conduct specified in section 203(e) of the Advisers Act, and you are not subject to an order, judgment or decree described in section 203(e) of the Advisers Act.

title: How to contact Albert
text: For immediate answers, chat with our virtual assistant here for guided support or check out our Help Center for answers to common questions. The fastest way to get help is by chatting with our virtual assistant , which can answer questions, help you navigate the app, and guide you through common actions. You can always ask to transfer to a live support agent to get continued support over text or email. Call us at (844) 891-9309 to listen to support options over the phone or leave a voicemail. To get help from within the app: Go to the profile tab ( 👤 ). Tap the menu icon in the top right (≡) Tap "Help" and let us know how we can help.

title: How do I repay cash advances?
text: Cash advances are due 6 days from when you initially advance. You may take out additional advances up to your limit in that time period. As necessary, you may also request up to a 7 day extension to your due date in the app. Instant Advance balances can be covered by making a manual repayment or automatically with Smart money deposits. Smart money deposits may not equal the amount of your Instant balance, and any amounts over will be deposited into your other Albert accounts. Albert also reserves the right to set off balances from your other Albert accounts to cover your advance balance. To make a manual payment: On the home screen, select "Instant Advance" Go to Settings (⚙️) Under the "Advance" section select "Make a manual payment" Follow the prompts to make a payment What happens if I don't repay by the due date? If your cash advance is not repaid within the agreed upon date, you may be suspended from accessing additional cash advances: If your cash advance is repaid within 15 days after the end of the due date, the suspension may be lifted when your covering deposits are completed. If your cash advance is repaid more than 15 days after the end of the due date, access to advances may be suspended for 30 days or more from when your repayment completes. If your cash advance is repaid more than 30 days after the end of the due date, access to advances may be suspended for 90 days or more from the day your repayment completes. Additional information The Instant Advance has no legal or contractual claim or remedy against you based on your failure to repay in the event the amount advanced is not repaid in full. Albert will not engage in any debt collection activities if your Instant advance is not repaid on the scheduled date, place the amount advanced as a debt with or sell it to a third party, or report to a consumer reporting agency concerning the amount advanced.

title: How do I qualify for cash advances?
text: Requirements We consider a variety of factors to determine your cash advance limit. We offer up to $1,000 with Instant and the amount available varies for eligible members based on each individual. A few things we consider: Account activity: an active bank account is linked to Albert Transaction history: an account with a long transaction history is linked to Albert Instant cash advance limits range from $25 to $1,000 and eligibility varies based on your ongoing account history and activity. Not all Albert customers will qualify and few qualify for $1,000. Other requirements Smart money set to the "Automatic" schedule is required to access Instant. You may turn this off by contacting customer support . If Smart money is turned off, you will no longer have access to Instant. An Albert Cash account is required to access Instant Advances.

title: How do I prioritize my Savings goals?
text: If you have automatic savings turned on with multiple savings goals, Albert will distribute your savings across your goals according to your priority settings. To prioritize Savings goals Tap on the Settings (⚙️) icon on the Savings screen. Tap on Adjust auto-saving . On the Saving settings screen under Savings goal priority , tap and drag the goal(s) to change their priority. This setting only appears if Savings is enabled and you have two or more savings goals. If you have multiple goals but only want to save toward a specific one, you can pause the other goals at any time. Learn more about pausing individual goals here .

title: How do I pause individual Savings goals?
text: Albert customers have the option to create and pause individual Savings goals. For example, you can pause goals if you prefer to save and fill up just one goal at a time, or if you don't necessarily want funds saved to the built-in Rainy day fund goal. At least one goal must be enabled for Albert to save for you. If you'd like to pause all savings, you can do so from the Savings setting screen. To pause a Savings goal On the home screen, tap Savings . Tap on the goal you want to pause. Under Utilities , tap the toggle next to Pause this goal . If your goals are filled or paused, future savings will deposit into the Rainy day fund ( )

title: How do I add money to Savings?
text: To deposit money into Savings: Go to the "Profile" tab (👤). Tap "Transfer money." Choose the account you're transferring money from. Choose "Savings" as the account you're sending money to. (You can select a specific Savings goal, or it will default to your "Rainy day fund.") Type your transfer amount and hit "Transfer." Savings transfers typically take 3–6 business days (Mon–Fri, excluding federal holidays) to complete. Any manually initiated Savings deposit(s) will not affect the amount Albert saves for you automatically each week. Read more about transfer times here .

title: How do I withdraw money from Savings?
text: To withdraw money from Savings: Go to the "Profile" tab (👤). Tap "Transfer money." Choose “Savings” as your “from” account and the account you’d like to transfer to. Enter the transfer amount and tap “Transfer.” You can only withdraw funds that have settled in your account. Deposits still in progress must first complete before you can withdraw your funds. For more information on transfer times, see here .

title: Managing your notifications
text: Albert may periodically send emails or push notifications regarding your Albert account. title: What is Albert Genius?
text: Albert Genius is your personal financial assistant. It’s an AI powered financial assistant that can help you budget and plan, move money instantly, help you shop, alert you about your finances, and more. How it works Genius puts your financial data to work to give you up-to-the-minute insight into your money and personalized suggestions for how to save, invest, and spend it. Then Genius acts on those suggestions for you, automatically. A financial planner Genius makes it simple to build budgets, track spending, and get insight into your financial innerworkings. At the end of each month, Genius also gives you a monthly report on your spending so you can track how you’re doing with your finances month-over-month. Personalized to you Genius analyzes your financial data, including your spending, income, recurring bills, and financial habits to make recommendations that are ultra personalized to you. Genius learns about you, your life, and what you like to make tailored recommendations that improve over time. Disclosures Albert Genius is a new type of financial assistant that uses generative AI to help you navigate your finances, set up a budget and financial plan, and answer general financial questions. You can also upload documents, which may include personal and financial information, to the Vault to be analyzed using AI, which can make mistakes. Albert Genius is not a licensed financial advisor. The information provided by and any non-investment related recommendations made by Albert Genius are intended for general information purposes only and are provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis. Such information and recommendations may not be comprehensive. When used for investing-related questions, Genius does not provide investment recommendations and cannot predict future investment performance. Genius is solely provided as a research tool to help locate publicly available disclosures and third-party research reports about investment opportunities selected by you. Genius does not independently verify the information it retrieves, which may contain factual errors. You should verify any information provided by Genius prior to making any investment decisions based on it. Genius is separate from the investment advisory services provided by Albert Investments, LLC, a registered investment adviser, which solely provides portfolio management services for customers who purchase its managed portfolios. You should review any information and recommendations provided by Genius carefully before taking action and consult with qualified financial and other advisors as needed. Such information and recommendations should not be construed as financial, legal or tax advice. Albert makes no representation or warranty as to any of the information or recommendations provided, in whole or in part, including with respect to their accuracy, reliability, timeliness, or content. Genius assistance Albert Genius uses generative AI which can make mistakes. Albert Genius can assist you and provide information about your linked accounts, including your Albert accounts, Albert services, and other financial tasks. However, it cannot affirmatively take action for you on its own with respect to such accounts, services, or tasks. If you need help with your Albert account or services, please reach out to customer support .

title: What can Albert Genius do?
text: Albert knows it all. Genius does it all. Albert Genius analyzes your spending, income, and recurring bills to make personalized financial recommendations, custom budgets, and much more. What Genius can do Send you monthly reports based on your spending and budget Create a long-term financial plan Transfer money between your accounts Create a travel itinerary for vacations and trips Find restaurants based on your location, or in a specific area Create custom notifications based on your financial data Answer any money question, and more

title: How do I set up forecasting?
text: Forecasting helps you plan and predict your financial future. It shows you how big expenses fit into your finances months ahead of time, so you can prepare without throwing off your monthly budget. To view your forecast: Go to the “Budgeting” tab Swipe over to “Forecast” Make any edits you’d like You can make changes to your account balances or growth assumptions and use our account and timeline filters to customize your view. Then, add events to your timeline so you can account for them in your long-term plans. To add events to your forecast timeline: Go to the “Budgeting” tab Swipe over to “Forecast” Tap “Add event” Give the event a name, amount, and set if it’s recurring or one-time Once you add events to your timeline, your future cash flow will reflect any dips or increases we expect these events will cause. What is net worth? Your net worth is calculated as your total assets minus liabilities. We predict your future net worth based on growth assumptions for those assets and liabilities, and you can view your net worth projections up to 5 years into the future. Assets Anything you own with economic value. For example: savings accounts and investments, like stocks and real estate. Liabilities oftentimes money owed to a lender, like credit cards and loans. How do I start forecasting? We use data from your linked accounts and your timeline to build out your forecast and help you plan for your financial future. Milestone tracking: Add big expenses (like a vacation or new car) to plan how they’ll fit into your budget. Timeline view: Visualize the months ahead and see when major expenses are expected to hit. Future cash estimates: See future account balances to estimate your future net worth. Detailed view: Understand how your accounts, spending, and debts shape our estimates of your future net worth. Fully customizable: Filter accounts, adjust timelines, and tailor your forecast to the perfect view for you. Genius guidance: Genius makes plans and suggestions to help you reach your financial goals.

title: What are cash advances?
text: To get started with Albert Instant advances, head to the home screen in the app or online and tap "Advances and loans." Follow the prompts to set up Instant. How do I advance cash? Once you've set up Instant, if you're eligible you can advance funds up to your limit. On the home screen, select “Advances and loans” Select “Albert Advance” Follow the prompts to complete your transfer Note: you can advance up to 6 times within a 30 day period. Where can I receive my advance? Your funds will be sent to your Albert Cash account. To set up Instant Advances a linked debit card is required. Albert will make a small (less than $0.40) transaction on your card and cancel it after verification. If your balance is less than $1, we'll delay this process until your balance increases to help avoid overdrafts. There are no late fees or interest for Albert Advances. An Albert subscription is not required to use Instant and has no impact on the amount that you're eligible for. The Instant Advance is subject to terms and eligibility requirements, including geographic restrictions. Albert Instant Advance The Instant Advance has no legal or contractual claim or remedy against you based on your failure to repay in the event the amount advanced is not repaid in full. Albert will not engage in any debt collection activities if your Instant advance is not repaid on the scheduled date, place the amount advanced as a debt with or sell it to a third party, or report to a consumer reporting agency concerning the amount advanced.

title: What is Albert Instant?
text: Albert Instant is an unsecured line of credit. You’ll have a borrowing limit you can draw from at any time. Draw fees may apply each time you advance, but only on the amount you borrow. When you open a line of credit with Instant: You can draw funds by requesting to send an advance to your Albert Cash account. These transfers will complete instantly. Instant limits range from $25-$1,000. Learn more about the Instant line of credit here . A subscription with Albert is not required to take out an Instant advance or Albert Loan.

title: What are Albert Loans?
text: Albert Loans are a personal loan you can apply for and use right away. The full loan amount is deposited upfront, and you pay interest on the entire balance over the life of the loan. You’ll be able to compare your term and APR options before submitting your application. When you take out a loan with Instant: You can receive your funds in your Albert Cash account instantly for no extra fee. Repayments for your loan are due based on your loan schedule over time. Information about your loan payments may be reported to consumer reporting agencies. A credit pull may be required to check your eligibility. Loan limits range from $1,000-$10,000. Learn more about Albert Loans here . A subscription with Albert is not required to take out an Instant advance or Albert Loan. Albert loans are issued by FinWise Bank, a Utah chartered commercial bank, Member FDIC.

title: How do I advance with Instant?
text: To get started with the Instant line of credit, head to the home screen in the app or online and tap “Instant.” Follow the prompts to set up Instant. How do I draw funds? Once you’ve set up Instant, if you’re eligible you can advance funds up to your limit. On the home screen, select “Borrow” Tap "Instant" Select an amount to advance Follow the prompts to complete your transfer Note: you can advance up to 6 times within a 30 day period. Where can I receive my funds? Your funds will be sent to your Albert Cash account, and will be available instantly after advancing. Draw fees may apply based on the amount of your transfer. To set up Instant a linked debit card is required. Albert will make a small (less than $0.40) transaction on your card and cancel it after verification. If your balance is less than $1, we’ll delay this process until your balance increases to help avoid overdrafts. The Instant line of credit is subject to terms and eligibility requirements, including geographic restrictions. If you move to a state where Instant line of credit is not offered, you will be unable to take additional draws from your Instant line of credit account during the time you reside in an ineligible state. However, you may be able to access other Instant products.

title: How do I qualify for advances with Instant?
text: Requirements We consider a variety of factors to determine your Instant line of credit limit. We offer advances up to $1,000 with Instant and the amount available varies for eligible members based on each individual. A few things we consider: Account activity: an active bank account is linked to Albert Transaction history: an account with a long transaction history is linked to Albert Consumer reporting: Albert obtains information from consumer reporting agencies Instant advance limits range from $25 to $1,000 and eligibility varies based on your ongoing account history and activity. Not all Albert customers will qualify and few qualify for $1,000. Do you check my credit? No, Albert does not pull your credit report to use Instant but does obtain other information from consumer reporting agencies.

title: How does Instant advance repayment work?
text: When your Instant repayment is due, it can be repaid by turning on auto pay or making a manual payment. To view your upcoming payments due: On the home screen, tap “Borrow” and select “Albert Instant” Go to Settings (⚙️) Select “Balance outstanding” View your upcoming payments due by amount and due date To temporarily pause auto pay: On the home screen, tap “Borrow” Select “Instant” Go to Settings (⚙️) Select “Pause auto pay” Select how long you want to pause for You can also contact support to temporarily pause or turn off auto pay at any time. To make a manual payment: On the home screen, select “Albert Instant” Go to Settings (⚙️) Select “Make a manual payment” Follow the prompts to make a payment What happens if I don’t repay by the due date? If your balance is not repaid within the agreed upon date, late fees may apply and you may be suspended from accessing additional draws on your line of credit: If your advance is repaid within 15 days after the end of the due date, the suspension may be lifted when your covering deposits are completed. If your advance is repaid more than 15 days after the end of the due date, access to advances may be suspended for 30 days or more from when your repayment completes. If your advance is repaid more than 30 days after the end of the due date, access to advances may be suspended for 90 days or more from the day your repayment completes.

title: $1,000 stock offer
text: Sign up to Albert and set up an Albert Investing account to see which stock you’ll receive. You’ll receive $1,000 in free stock in your Albert Investing account and can claim it after depositing funds and meeting the requirements below. How it works By signing up for an Albert Investing account, you’ll learn which randomly-selected stock you will be eligible for upon satisfying the program requirements. To receive $1,000 worth of this stock, you must complete the following: Complete the signup flow to create an Albert account Sign up for the Genius AI subscription tier Create an Albert Investing account Deposit at least $10,000 within 90 days of opening your account (the “Minimum Deposit”) Maintain a Genius AI subscription plan and keep your Albert account in good standing for a continuous period of at least 12 months from the date you created your Albert Investing account (such period, the “Subscription Period”) Maintain the Minimum Deposit, not including the free stock award, in your Albert Investing account through the end of your Subscription Period, following the date you first funded your investing account with the Minimum Deposit. Maintaining the Minimum Deposit means the sum of your deposits must always exceed the sum of your withdrawals by at least $10,000. Any gains or losses on your investments do not affect this calculation. When you open your Albert Investing account, your free stock will show as “locked” and will be unavailable to sell until the date all requirements set forth above have been met. Your free stock is granted and priced as of the close of market on the day you first meet the Minimum Deposit requirements. The value of the stock will show as $1,000 prior to this date. Once the stock is granted, it will reflect the market value of the stock and the value may increase or decrease based on that value. The cost basis for the free stock is one thousand dollars ($1,000) in the form of the free stock securities as determined by the fair market value as of the close of market on the day it is granted or if granted on a day the market is not open, the close of business of the last trading day. Receipt of the free stock may result in the incurrence of tax and you are responsible for payment of any such tax. Please consult your tax advisors for any potential tax consequences. The free stock will become available to sell, or to continue holding without restriction after the 12 month hold period has ended and you’ve met all requirements listed above. While the free stock gift is locked, it will show as part of your investing account balance. This amount does not apply to the $10,000 Minimum Deposit requirement. You can check the status of the requirements to unlock your stock when viewing your gift stock transaction from Investing. If you fail to meet any of these requirements, the full amount of the free stock, including any gains or losses, will revert to Albert. Eligibility To be eligible for the free stock offer, you must be a first-time Albert Investing customer. Existing and previous Albert Investing customers are not eligible for this offer. This offer cannot be combined with other Albert offers or discounts for signing up or opening an Albert Investing account. Offer valid through 6/30/27. Only Owners and not Members of a Family Plan subscription (as such terms are defined in Albert's Terms of Use) are eligible for this offer. Please note that Albert may terminate this offer or change any of the eligibility or other criteria or terms of the offer at any time or from time to time in its sole discretion. Stock gift disclosures The value of the free stock granted to you as part of this offer is not guaranteed and may increase or decrease prior to your being allowed to sell it. The free stock is likely to include a fractional quantity of shares, which when multiplied by the current market price at the time the stock is awarded is equal to $1,000. Fractional shares cannot be transferred to other brokerage firms and can only be sold through Albert. The free stock award does not constitute a recommendation to invest in the stock awarded. Albert Securities does not make any recommendations and Albert Investments only makes recommendations to purchasers of its managed portfolios. Additional limitations on the investment-related services offered by Albert are discussed here . Individuals employed by Albert Corporation, its banking partners, affiliated companies, and/or subsidiaries, at the time their Albert account is first opened and members of their immediate family (parent, child, sibling or spouse) or persons living in the same household are not eligible for this offer. title: When will my funds be available?
text: The time it takes for transfers to process will depend on the type of transfer and which accounts the money is being sent to and from. The times below are estimates based on Albert’s processing times. There may be additional factors that delay posting your transfer, which can include your external’s bank’s policies or our own fraud prevention policies. Transfers between Albert Cash and external bank accounts Transfers between Cash and external bank accounts are completed via ACH transfer, a bank-to-bank transfer. Estimated time to securely process transfers between Albert Cash and an external bank account: Deposits: 5–6 business days (excluding weekends and holidays) Withdrawals: 2–3 business days (excluding weekends and holidays) Setting up direct deposit with your Albert Cash account can help reduce your ACH transfer processing times to 2–3 business days. Transfers between Albert Savings and external bank accounts Transfers between Savings and external bank accounts are completed via ACH transfer, a bank-to-bank transfer. Estimated time to securely process transfers between Albert Savings and an external bank account: Deposits: 5–6 business days (excluding weekends and holidays) Withdrawals: 2–3 business days (excluding weekends and holidays) Transfers between Albert Investing and external bank accounts Transfers between Investing and external bank accounts are completed via ACH transfer, a bank-to-bank transfer. Estimated time to securely process transfers between Albert Investing and an external bank account: Deposits: 5–8 business days (excluding weekends and holidays) Withdrawals: 2–3 business days (excluding weekends and holidays) Funds from sales take 2 business days to settle before they can be withdrawn. For security purposes, deposits made into your Albert Investing account include an additional 5 business day holding period before they can be withdrawn. Transfers between Albert products In most cases, transfers between Albert accounts are available immediately. Direct deposit If you have direct deposit set up with Albert, your paycheck will be posted as soon as we receive it from your payroll provider. You may have access to your paycheck up to 2 days early compared to other banks. Read more about how early pay works here . Business days and ACH transfers ACH transfers are bank-to-bank transfers. Meaning, that they are transferred between Albert and your externally linked bank account. These transfers are processed through the Automated Clearing House (ACH) Network. Transfers made over ACH are processed on weekdays and business days (when banks are open), and are not processed on weekends or federal holidays. The time it takes to process your transfer can be extended due to processing times that are over weekends, federal holidays, or any other additional holding periods. Business days typically include: Weekdays, Monday through Friday Business days exclude: Weekends, Saturday and Sunday Federal holidays Note: Transactions initiated after 4pm PT will be considered received the following business day.

title: What if I notice an error with an Albert card transaction?
text: In most cases, the fastest way to resolve an issue is likely to directly contact the merchant who can often cancel or reverse the transaction. If you see a transaction you didn't authorize, we are happy to look into that for you. Read more on how. Here’s what to do if you experience one of the following issues: I was overcharged in a pending transaction. Restaurants, hotels, and gas stations will typically place a temporary hold on your card to ensure there’s sufficient credit to cover the expense. Your card hasn’t been charged yet, since the merchant doesn’t know the final amount of the actual sale (that is, the amount you actually spent at an establishment). Usually, it takes merchants up to 3 days to release the hold. Gas stations can hold up to $125 when you use your card at the pump. Usually, they release the hold within 2 hours, but it can take up to 4 days. To avoid this situation, we recommend paying for your gas inside at the register. A transaction should have been canceled but is still pending. A pending non-travel, non-hospitality transaction can remain on your account for up to 8 days before it is canceled by the merchant. For travel and hospitality merchants, the cancelation can take even longer — up to 30 days. If the cancelation hasn’t been processed after that period, please contact the merchant directly to get help with this issue. I don’t recognize a transaction. First, freeze your card in the app. Here's how to freeze your card: From the home screen, tap "Checking." Tap the image of your debit card. Under the "Features" section, switch the toggle button to "Freeze card." You can submit a dispute claim in the app by tapping “Report an issue” on the transactions page once the transaction has settled. For more assistance, you can always chat with our virtual support agent .

title: ATM fees, reimbursements and waivers
text: Albert is part of the Allpoint ATM network which has over 55,000 ATM locations around the U.S. that are in-network ($0 withdrawal fees) when you subscribe to Albert Genius. You can find these ATMs in the app. When you use an out-of-network ATM, two fees can apply: Albert's out-of-network fee ($3.50), and a surcharge the ATM operator charges with the withdrawal. Albert will waive out-of-network ATM fees and reimburse certain fees charged by ATM operators (together, a “Fee Reimbursement”) for customers that opt in to the feature and meet the eligibility requirements below. To enable ATM fee reimbursements in the app: From the home screen or checking screen, look for the "Enable ATM Fee reimbursement" alert. You must meet the eligibility requirements below to see this alert. Tap Enable. Review the terms and confirm. Your account will be re-checked for eligibility. If it no longer qualifies, you'll see an error and can contact support. Albert out-of-network ATM fee waiver Once you opt in, Albert's own out-of-network ATM fee is not charged, including on international withdrawals. You won't see a separate transaction; the withdrawal is the only charge. Operator surcharge rebate Third-party ATM operators sometimes add their own surcharge, built into the total amount withdrawn. For eligible accounts, that surcharge is credited back as a separate transaction shortly after the withdrawal settles. Conditions US withdrawals only — international or non-USD withdrawals aren't eligible for the operator fee reimbursement (the Albert out-of-network fee waiver will still apply) Operator fee reimbursements are capped at $20 per bank account per calendar month Individual operator fee reimbursements are capped at $9.99 per transaction Eligibility To be eligible for ATM Fee Reimbursements, you must meet the following requirements: Subscribe to Genius AI or a family tier and remain current on subscription payments Your Albert Cash account must have Qualifying direct deposits, with at least $500 received in the last 40 days, OR Albert Cash balance of $1,000 or more Opt in to the feature Eligibility is evaluated at the account level, not per user or card. Albert assesses all eligibility requirements on an ongoing basis and your ATM Fee Reimbursement may be disabled if you no longer meet one of the requirements. Joint accounts are only eligible if every account holder meets the subscription requirement. The qualifying direct deposit must be made by your employer, payroll provider, or benefits payer by Automated Clearing House (ACH deposit). Bank ACH transfers, federal, state, or local tax refunds or credits, federal or state unemployment short-term disability, or social security benefits are not qualifying direct deposits. Rental payments from Airbnb, VRBO, Turo, or other similar services are not qualifying direct deposits. Mobile check deposits, peer-to-peer transfers from services like Cash App, Venmo, Wise, or PayPal, business account transfers or deposits, 1099 related deposits, or other similar deposits are not qualifying direct deposits.
